newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to solve Red Army case in 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to solve Red Army case in 24 hours.

text.p: Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Friday the case of Japanese Red Army suspects reported held in Lebanon, an issue mired in confusion for the past 11 days, would be solved within 24 hours.

"The case of the Japanese is nearing completion after all the information over this matter was collected. All the necessary measures will be taken to end this case within the next 24 hours," Bouez told reporters in Beirut.
"The solution will ripen tonight," he added.

Japan's Ambassador in Beirut Yasuji Ishigaki said after meeting Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri that the Lebanese government would cooperate fully with Japan to identify the detainees who could possibly include Japanese citizens.

"The Lebanese authorities have under custody some Asian nationals including possibly Japanese nationals and he (Hariri) said that he would see to it that the prosecutor general in accordance with Lebanese law and regulations would give us full cooperation to identify them," Ishigaki told reporters.
"I was told that these people will be dealt with through the Lebanese law and regulations," he added.

The case has been shrouded in confusion since February 18 when Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in Tokyo that Lebanese officials had told him six Japanese Red Army suspects had been arrested in eastern Lebanon's Bekaa Valley.
Lebanese officials have been tight-lipped since Hashimoto's statement, apart from Bouez who said publicly on the same day that arrests of Japanese Red Army members had taken place.

Confusion mounted this week when Interior Minister Michel al-Murr and Lebanese security sources said no Lebanese security or military intelligence agency was holding any Japanese detainees. Judicial sources said they were sure that Syrian troops in Lebanon were not holding the Japanese.

The Beirut daily an-Nahar on Friday quoted Justice Minister Bahij Tabbara as saying: "I have asked Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum to...inform me fully on this subject and I hope all the information will be ready by Saturday."

The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. The Bekaa Valley was a haven during Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war for guerrilla groups including Lebanese Moslems and Marxists, Palestinians, Kurds and the Red Army.
